sources.build_takeaway: Prompts should specify concrete output shape and constraints; the CLI prompt contract verifier turns that into a prelaunch guard.
Codex CLI approval/sandbox modes are operational surfaces; launch receipts should continue to record read-only route, no-babysitting gate, and temp-only raw boundaries.
Connector and tool flows should minimize scope and prevent token/session confusion; status receipts should avoid raw transport and private identifiers.
Token audience and passthrough boundaries map to THOS connector-boundary records and app-lane redaction before publication.
Logs and receipts should be structured and useful while avoiding sensitive data, alarm fog, and unredacted identifiers.
